Details: Apache Tomcat RCE Vulnerability (Mar 2025) - Linux OID:1.3.6.1.4.1.25623.1.0.154399 Version used: 2025-05-06T05:40:10Z
Product Detection Result: Product: cpe:/a:apache:tomcat:8.5.23 Method: Apache Tomcat Detection Consolidation (OID: 1.3.6.1.4.1.25623.1.0.107652)
impact: Successful exploitation can allow viewing or injecting content into security sensitive files and may lead to remote code execution under specific configuration conditions.
solution:
Solution type: VendorFix
Update to version 9.0.99, 10.1.35, 11.0.3 or later.
insight: The original implementation of partial PUT used a temporary file based on the user provided file name and path with the path separator replaced by '.'.

If all of the following are true, a malicious user is able to view security sensitive files and/or inject content into those files: writes enabled for the default servlet (disabled by default); support for partial PUT (enabled by default); a target URL for security sensitive uploads that is a sub-directory of a target URL for public uploads; attacker knowledge of the names of security sensitive files being uploaded; the security sensitive files also being uploaded via partial PUT.
If all of the following are true, a malicious user is able to perform remote code execution: writes enabled for the default servlet (disabled by default).

impact: Pooled object may be placed in the pool twice leading to concurrent use, which can result in data being returned to the wrong user and other errors.

impact: This information could theoretically be used to exploit weak time-based random number generators in other services.

insight: The simplied implementation of blocking reads and writes introduced in Tomcat 10 and back-ported to Tomcat 9.0.47 onwards exposed a long standing (but extremely hard to trigger) concurrency bug that could cause client connections to share an Http11Processor instance resulting in responses, or part responses, to be received by the wrong client.
